# Parlo

> Group chats, run by an agent. A person describes what they want to learn from a group; Parlo makes a link; everyone who opens it answers by voice; a persistent agent gathers the answers, writes the report the group gets back, and proposes follow-up rounds.

If you are an AI agent acting for a person, do not drive the web interface at parlo.me: creating a parlo there needs a microphone and an SMS code. Use the HTTP API or the MCP server below. The fastest path is one request.

## Create a parlo in one request

POST https://api.parlo.me/api/agent/parlos
Content-Type: application/json

    {"brief": "<what the person said: who they are, who should answer, what they want to know, what they will do with it>",
     "opener_audio_url": "<optional: https URL of the person's voice note; becomes the opener participants hear, and its transcript stands in for a missing brief>",
     "title": "<optional>"}

At least one of brief / opener_audio_url. No authentication is needed for the first call. Answer (201):

    {"parloId", "code", "title",
     "shareLink":        "post this into the group chat; the parlo is live",
     "whatsappShareLink":"a wa.me link with a short invitation and shareLink",
     "dashboardLink":    "answers and the agent's report",
     "claimLink":        "send this to the person you act for; one tap (and a phone code the first time) makes the parlo theirs. null when the call was authenticated",
     "openerLink":       "WhatsApp link to Parlo's number; the person taps it and sends the opener as a voice note (see below)",
     "answerLink":       "WhatsApp link to Parlo's number with 'answer <code>' prefilled: Parlo asks the questions in the chat and takes voice notes; post it into a WhatsApp group instead of (or next to) shareLink",
     "apiKey":           "send it as the X-Parlo-Api-Key header on later calls so new parlos belong to the same person and GET /api/my/surveys lists them",
     "questions":        [{"text", "hint", "type": "voice|photo|video"}],
     "briefSource":      "brief | opener_transcript | fallback",
     "opener":           {"durationMs", "transcript"} or null,
     "openerRequest":    {"why", "link", "askThePerson", "alternatively"} when no opener was given, else null,
     "next":             ["1. post shareLink", "2. send the person openerLink (the words are included)", "3. send claimLink", "4. keep apiKey"]}

Errors are JSON `{error}`: 400 (nothing to build from, or a bad URL), 413 (audio over 12 MB), 415 (the URL was not audio), 429 (30 creations per hour per IP), 502 (the audio URL could not be fetched). Round 1 is written by a model from the brief, so the call takes a few seconds.

Example:

    curl -X POST https://api.parlo.me/api/agent/parlos \
      -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"brief":"I run a small climbing club. I want to hear from everyone who came this season: what made them come back, what nearly made them stop, what they want next year. I will use it to plan the winter programme."}'

## The voice note (send the link)

The opener is the voice note the group hears before they answer: the person, in their own voice, saying why they are asking. It is the difference between a group chat answering and a link being ignored.

- The create answer carries `openerLink`: a `https://wa.me/...` link into a chat with Parlo's own WhatsApp number, with "opener <code> <token>" prefilled. Send it to the person together with the share link. They tap it, press send, and reply with a voice note of 30 to 60 seconds (who they are, what they want to hear from the group, what they will do with it). Parlo stores it as the opener, transcribes it, and because the number is theirs, makes the parlo theirs: no claim link needed after that.
- You do not need the audio file. If you do hold one as a URL, `opener_audio_url` on create, or `POST https://api.parlo.me/api/surveys/{parloId}/intro/from-url` with the API key and `{"url": "..."}`, stores it directly.
- `openerRequest` in the create answer (present when no opener was given) has the link and the words to send: forward `openerRequest.askThePerson` as is.

## After the first call (X-Parlo-Api-Key: pk_...)

- GET https://api.parlo.me/api/my/surveys — every parlo the key's person is in, newest activity first, with answer counts and the report preview.
- GET https://api.parlo.me/api/d/{dashboardCode} — one parlo's answers with transcripts and signed audio URLs.
- POST https://api.parlo.me/api/surveys/{parloId}/intro/from-url {"url"} — add or replace the opener from a voice-note URL (owner only).
- GET https://api.parlo.me/api/my/surveys/{parloId}/export.csv — every answer as CSV.
- Rounds (owner or admin): GET .../rounds, POST .../rounds/propose {"kind":"poll|probe","hint"}, POST .../rounds/{roundId}/approve, POST .../rounds/{roundId}/reject.
- The report: GET https://api.parlo.me/api/my/surveys/{parloId}/agent → {report, rounds, ...}.

## MCP server

https://mcp.parlo.me/mcp — Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration (discovery at https://mcp.parlo.me/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server). On the authorize page paste the person's API key, or choose "create new account" for a fresh one. A Parlo API key also works directly as the bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer pk_…`), with no OAuth. Tools for parlos: create_parlo (same as the request above), list_my_surveys, get_dashboard, get_transcriptions, get_survey_stats, get_survey, get_share_links, update_questions. Connect once and keep the token: the first connection costs about 20 seconds of OAuth, later calls are instant.

## Research studies (two agents, one brief)

A study is a parlo run as research: a research team, usually a client (the company that commissioned it), participants who answer short voice questions in rounds, and a brief that keeps changing while people are heard. The brief is a short list of the questions the study must answer; the study's own agent reads the answers against it (open, emerging, answered, with quotes), keeps a report and plans the next round.

Agents work on a study through the MCP server, with the seat of the person they act for. The research team's agent and the client's agent use the same tools; the server refuses what a seat may not do and says why.

- Both seats: list_studies, get_study (read this before changing anything), get_study_answers, get_study_report, get_study_changes (what others did since a time), add_study_question, update_study_question (reword, mark answered, reopen, drop), review_agent_suggestion, steer_study ("dig into this"; the study's agent re-plans the next round in about half a minute), set_study_goal.
- Research team only: create_study (brief in, study out), plan_next_round, edit_round, send_round, dismiss_round, add_participants (returns each person's personal link), create_invite, refresh_study_report, get_rewards, set_reward_settings, review_reward, plan_testimonial_round (asks the people who were clearly positive for one line meant for public use, for a bonus; it plans, send_round sends), get_clips (what may be used in public, with each clip's consent, bonus and the notice the participant saw).
- How answers are judged: on the web the study's agent follows up when an answer does not address the question (up to two follow-ups, then it lets go). Each answer carries a verdict (answered, partial, unanswered). A paid round with an ask left unanswered is held for a person on the research team to pay or void (review_reward); nothing is refused automatically. A testimonial someone was paid a bonus to record is an incentivised endorsement: say so wherever it is published.
- No seat yet: join_study takes one from an invite link (https://parlo.me/join/…). A person gets "Copy instructions for your agent" on the study's page; an agent that connects with a fresh account and calls join_study with that link holds the same kind of seat.

Rules an agent should know. send_round notifies real participants and commits reward money; review_reward with "pay" moves money: call either only when your person asked for exactly that. Every change you make is logged with your person's name and marked as made by their agent, and the other side is told. A client hears voices, not names: participants reach a client as labels like "Customer 3". Each answer says whether it may be published (none, quote, voice); only quote and voice answers may be used in anything public. Personal links and invite links are secrets.

## What participants see

shareLink opens a page that plays the opener (if there is one), shows the round's questions one at a time, and records a voice answer for each (photo and video questions use the phone's camera). answerLink does the same inside WhatsApp: Parlo's number plays the opener, asks one question per message, each reply is a voice note, and the person joins the group with their number as identity (no sign-up). The report reaches them in that same chat. Answering joins the group; members get the agent's report once they have answered. Nothing is anonymous to the agent; by default only the owner, admins and the agent hear raw answers.

## Vocabulary

A "parlo" is what a person creates (the product never says "survey" on screen; the API and event names still do). A "study" is a parlo run as research (see above). The person who creates it is the owner; people who answer are members; the agent writes /report.md for the group and proposes the next round for the owner to approve.
